the science of your kid’s brain, made simple

Your kid didn’t come with a manual. Here’s the code.

Meltdowns. Bad sleep. “I’m bored.” The 5 p.m. hangry explosion. A teen who stopped talking. It looks like a dozen different problems. It’s the same few messengers, hormones and brain parts, plus a handful of habits getting in their way. We turned the science into a cartoon crew, so you can see what’s going on and know what to try tonight. No pills. No guesswork. No 300-page books.

hi, we’re the Little Brain Crew!

12 hard moments.
The same few causes.

What looks like “bad behavior” is almost always a signal. These are the 12 moments parents tell us about most. Find the one you see at home.

  • Tears or yelling when screen time endsDopa just lost its easy rewards. Villain: Lupi.
  • “I’m bored.” Won’t start homework or clean-up.Nora’s spotlight won’t switch on. Villain: Pingi.
  • Explodes over small thingsMigo yelled “danger!” before Fronti had time to think.
  • Can’t wait: grabs, interrupts, blurts it outFronti’s brakes are still under construction.
  • Melts down the minute they’re home from schoolGreli is ringing the hunger bell, and Corti held it in all day.
  • Wired at bedtime, grumpy at breakfastMela showed up late. Villains: Glo and Bedi.
  • Can’t fall asleep, worries at nightGabi can’t find the brake while Corti is still on.
  • Bouncing off the walls at 9 p.m.Endo never got to run today.
  • Doesn’t listen until you yellToci needs a moment of connection before the instruction.
  • Sibling fights, every single dayToci feels there isn’t enough of you to go around.
  • Cranky all week when the routine falls apartSero likes days that look the same. Villain: Lati.
  • A teen with no energy and no confidenceTeo needs sleep, sport and daylight.
It’s a code.

Not a bad kid. Not bad parenting. A small crew doing its job, and a few villains getting in the way. Learn who’s talking, and you know what to try tonight.

Meet the
Little Brain Crew.

Every character is a real messenger, hormone or part of the brain with a real job. Tap one: what it does, what helps it, what throws it off, and how to bring it back to calm. We’ve mapped 156 of them. A new one joins the crew every month.

The characters are a way to explain behavior, not a measurement of your child’s chemistry. No single chemical “causes” a mood; they all work as a team. This is for learning, built on everyday habits. It is not medical advice. If you are worried about your child’s sleep, mood, growth or behavior, talk to your pediatrician.

the science behind every habit

Two rules run your kid’s brain.

No willpower speeches. No 47-step routines. Just two things the research keeps coming back to.

Rule 1 · Plasti

The brain changes from what’s repeated.

Every bedtime at the same time and every screen ending done the same way carves the path a little deeper. Scientists call it neuroplasticity, and it’s strongest in childhood. That’s why one small habit, repeated, beats one big talk.

Rule 2 · Duo

Kids borrow your calm before they can make their own.

A calm grown-up close by helps a child’s body settle. Scientists call it co-regulation. Your kid learns to calm down by doing it with you, hundreds of times. In this crew, that’s you. You’re Duo.

Meet the villains stealing
your kid’s sleep and focus.

They’re not people, and they’re not your kid. They’re habits and things that sneak into every house. Each one has a simple way to beat it. Hover one to watch it lose.

Is this normal at 3?
At 14?

Every age has its own character. Here’s what’s normal right now, and where to put your energy. Ages are approximate. Every kid has their own pace.

Questions before you start

Which one should I get?

All three are opening soon. The Kid Brain Toolkit ($9) is for understanding what’s going on, in one evening. The 30-Day Reset ($39) walks you through it, one small habit a day, and includes the Toolkit. The Crew Club adds new crew members and answers as your kid grows.

Where does the science come from?

From published research and pediatric guidelines on sleep, light, movement, screens, food and closeness. We name our sources. We keep every claim no bigger than the study behind it, and we explain behavior, we don’t diagnose it.

Will you add more crew members?

Yes. We’ve mapped 156 messengers, hormones, brain parts, senses and habits that shape a kid. A new one joins the crew every month, and Crew Club members get each one first.

What ages is it for?

Kids 3 to 17. Every age has its own stage character, from Whyzi (3–6) to Seki (14–17). Teo, our teen character, shows up in the teen material.

When does it open?

Soon. We’re finishing the last setup. Leave your email for the free tips and we’ll tell you the day it opens. After that, your link lands in your inbox within a minute of paying, to watch or read on your phone, tablet or TV.

Can I get a refund?

Once we open, you get instant access to digital content, so all sales will be final. If something doesn’t work, like a link or a file that won’t open, email us and we’ll fix it fast. The Crew Club is different: pause or cancel it yourself, anytime, in 2 clicks.

Is it a subscription?

No. The Toolkit and the 30-Day Reset are one payment and yours to keep. Only the Crew Club is monthly or yearly, and you can pause or cancel it yourself.

Do you sell pills or supplements?

Never. No supplements, hormones, medicine or body products. Only habits: sleep, daylight, food, movement, play, closeness and smarter screen time.

Is this medical advice?

No. It’s learning for parents. We don’t diagnose, treat or promise results. If something worries you, your pediatrician is the right first call.
